findings.issue: The time adverb 'hoy' is produced from EN 'today' in 9 sentence `es` strings (s.02, s.04, s.05, s.06, s.07, s.08, s.11, s.12, s.13) plus the passage, yet 'hoy' is NOT in the curriculum-map's free-glue list (degree/quantity adverbs listed are muy/más/poco/mucho/bien/mal — time adverbs are not enumerated), is not a VocabItem, and carries no vocabRef. ('mucho' is genuinely free glue, so it is fine.) This is defensible under the a1-02 free-adverb precedent but the most-repeated non-verb word in the lesson enters untaught and undocumented. Cite: Style Guide §3 vocab-leakage discipline vs. Curriculum-Map glue policy (non-exhaustive free list). Same issue the r1 gate logged as documentation-only rather than fixed.
findings.proposedFix: Record 'hoy' in the Curriculum-Map glue policy (add time adverbs, or explicitly list 'hoy') and note it in the a1-03 QA notes as an intentionally-free adverb; no content change to the lesson required.

findings.issue: Difficulty distribution is 0×L1, 7×L2, 4×L3, 2×L4, 1×L5 — it clusters at level 2 (half the lesson) and has NO level-1 sentence at all. Style Guide §3 asks the 12-20 sentences to 'spread across the range; don't cluster at 3' (here the cluster is at 2, with an empty low end). The lesson's shortest item, s.03 '¿Dónde trabajas?', is rated 2 (defensible: question-formation + pronoun-drop trap), so no true L1 content exists.
findings.proposedFix: Add or re-rate one short, alternate-free item toward L1 (e.g. a bare '¿Trabajas?' / 'Descanso.' style prompt) so the low end is represented, or accept the skew as inherent to a conjugation-drill lesson and note it as advisory.
